## When People Decide with [AI]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
When an AI teammate advises people in dynamic, high-stakes tasks, human–AI teaming research asks:
:::

:::: {.research-grid .question-cards}

::: {.research-question}
[Trust and reliance]{.research-topic}

When do people follow AI advice, and when is that reliance appropriate?
:::

::: {.research-question}
[Decisions under pressure]{.research-topic}

How do uncertainty and time constraints affect reliance?
:::

::: {.research-question}
[Situation awareness]{.research-topic}

What happens when the person and AI have access to different information?
:::

::: {.research-question}
[Cognitive state]{.research-topic}

How does AI advice affect attention and workload?
:::

::: {.research-question}
[AI teammate design]{.research-topic}

Which teammate behaviors and communication strategies improve team performance?
:::

::: {.research-question}
[Adaptive assistance]{.research-topic}

When should assistance change with task demands or human performance?
:::

::::

::: {.punchline}
Answering these questions requires observing the interaction [as it unfolds over time]{.accent}.
:::

::: {.notes}
These are the field's core questions. Each one plays out during the interaction,
as decisions, advice, and consequences build on each other.
:::

---

## What Is [MOSAIC]{.accent}?

::: {.hook}
MOSAIC (Modular System for Adaptive Human–AI Collaboration) is an open-source Python platform for studying human–AI teaming through configurable tasks.
:::

::::: {.need-map .linked}

:::: {.need-column}

::: {.need-item .has-visual}
::: {.need-visual .thumb}
![](assets/game-view.png){fig-alt="One room of the search-and-rescue task: lava, a victim, and doors."}
:::

::: {.need-text}
[01]{.need-index}

[Interactive task]{.need-title}

A search-and-rescue mission where each move changes what the participant can do next.
:::
:::

::: {.need-item .has-visual}
::: {.need-visual .thumb .pair}
![](assets/cam-room.png){fig-alt="A room shown with the room camera."} ![](assets/cam-cone.png){fig-alt="The same room shown with the cone camera."}
:::

::: {.need-text}
[03]{.need-index}

[Configurable conditions]{.need-title}

Map, hazards, camera view, scoring, and feedback are set per study, without changing the package.
:::
:::

::::

```{=html}
<div class="need-links" aria-hidden="true"><svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none">
  <line x1="50" y1="50" x2="0" y2="24"/><line x1="50" y1="50" x2="0" y2="76"/>
  <line x1="50" y1="50" x2="100" y2="24"/><line x1="50" y1="50" x2="100" y2="76"/>
</svg></div>
```

::: {.need-core}
[MOSAIC]{.need-core-title}

[one configurable testbed]{.need-core-subtitle}
:::

:::: {.need-column}

::: {.need-item .has-visual}
::: {.need-visual .thumb}
![](assets/chat-advice.png){fig-alt="The chat panel with the teammate's reply: Survivor to the north-east, about 3 steps away."}
:::

::: {.need-text}

Scripted or LLM teammates behind one interface. Set what it sees, how reliable it is, and when it speaks.

::: {.need-visual .thumb}

::: {.need-text}
[04]{.need-index}

[Synchronized data]{.need-title}

Game events, AI advice, and sensor streams such as gaze share one clock through LSL.
:::

::::

:::::

::: {.punchline}
MOSAIC brings these capabilities together in [one configurable experimental platform]{.accent}.
:::

::: {.notes}
MOSAIC stands for Modular System for Adaptive Human–AI Collaboration. Like a mosaic
built from tiles, it assembles separate parts (task, teammate, interface, sensing)
into one study. Each box answers the need in the same position on the last slide:
the task, a teammate you can control, conditions you set per study, and one
synchronized record.
:::

## How [MOSAIC]{.accent} Works

::: {.hook}
Each part is a separate module: the participant acts on the task, the AI teammate advises from task context, and LSL aligns every stream into one session record.
:::

::: {.overview-diagram}
::: {.system-row}

::: {.system-node}
[Human participant]{.system-title}

Observes, decides, and acts.
:::

::: {.system-link .two-way}
[actions]{.link-top}

[observations]{.link-bottom}
:::

::: {.system-node .system-core}
[MOSAIC task]{.system-title}

Runs the task and the human-facing interface.
:::

::: {.system-link .two-way}
[task context]{.link-top}

[advice]{.link-bottom}
:::

::: {.system-node}
[AI teammate]{.system-title}

Interprets task context and provides advice.
:::

:::

::: {.drop-row}

::: {.record-drop}
[physiological signals]{.record-drop-label}
:::

::: {.record-drop}
[task and interaction stream]{.record-drop-label}
:::

:::

::: {.sync-row}

::: {.sync-node}
[Study sensors]{.system-title}

Physiological data: EEG, eye tracking, pupil diameter
:::

::: {.sync-link}
Time-stamped stream
:::

::: {.sync-node .sync-core}
[Lab Streaming Layer (LSL)]{.system-title}

Aligns streams on a shared clock
:::

::: {.sync-link}
Synchronized record
:::

::: {.sync-node .system-record}
[Session data]{.system-title}

Ready for analysis and replay
:::

:::
:::

::: {.notes}
Here is MOSAIC. You're the participant on the left. You act, the task updates, and
when you ask, the teammate reads the task context and answers. Everything the
researcher varies sits in configuration, and everything that happens, including gaze
and physiology, lands on one clock. Underneath, the reusable parts live in the
`mosaic` package and each study's choices live in `experiment/`; the code map at
the end shows that split.
:::

## The Task: [Search and Rescue]{.accent}

:::: {.columns .scenario-columns}

::: {.column width="58%"}
![](assets/cam-full.png){height="430" fig-align="center"}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}

::: {.scenario-brief}
[Mission]{.scenario-label}

Search a multiroom building and rescue the real victims.

[Sources of difficulty]{.scenario-label}

- Locked rooms require the correct key
- Lava constrains safe routes
- Configurations can add decoys and health pressure
- Time and step limits create urgency
:::

:::

::::

::: {.punchline}
Search and rescue provides a controlled but [consequential setting]{.accent} for studying human–AI decisions.
:::

## The Human–AI [Teaming Loop]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
At every decision, the participant can act alone or ask for advice.
:::

::: {.teaming-diagram}

::: {.loop-return}
[next decision]{.arrow-label}
:::

::: {.loop-main}

::: {.loop-node}
[1]{.decision-number} [Observe]{.decision-title}

Read the room and the mission state.
:::

::: {.loop-arrow}
:::

::: {.loop-node .loop-choice}
[2]{.decision-number} [Decide]{.decision-title}

Act alone, or ask the AI teammate.
:::

::: {.loop-arrow}
[act alone]{.arrow-label}
:::

::: {.loop-node}
[3]{.decision-number} [Act]{.decision-title}

The participant always chooses the final action.
:::

::: {.loop-arrow}
:::

::: {.loop-node}
[4]{.decision-number} [Outcome]{.decision-title}

The environment updates and the score changes.
:::

:::

::: {.advice-branch}

::: {.branch-label}
Optional advice path
:::

::: {.branch-down}
[ask]{.arrow-label}
:::

::: {.branch-up}
[use or ignore]{.arrow-label}
:::

::: {.advice-box .ask}
[Request advice]{.advice-box-title}

MOSAIC sends task context to the AI teammate.
:::

::: {.loop-arrow .branch-across}
[advice]{.arrow-label}
:::

::: {.advice-box .evaluate}
[Evaluate advice]{.advice-box-title}

Compare it with what the participant can see.
:::

:::

:::

::: {.cycle-band}
[Recorded throughout]{.cycle-title} Task state · advice request · AI response · participant action · outcome
:::

::: {.punchline}
The central question is when and how AI advice [changes human decisions]{.accent}.
:::

::: {.notes}
Next, we will install MOSAIC, run the included experiment, and then build one
small study with it.
:::

## Clone MOSAIC and Create the [Environment]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Everything in the tutorial runs from one repository and one environment.
:::

:::: {.columns .install-split}

::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.panel-tabset .install-code}

### macOS / Linux

```bash
git clone https://github.com/iHuman-Lab/mosaic.git
cd mosaic
python3 -m venv mosaic_env
source mosaic_env/bin/activate
```

### Windows PowerShell

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/iHuman-Lab/mosaic.git
cd mosaic
python -m venv mosaic_env
.\mosaic_env\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

### Conda · Any Platform

```bash
git clone https://github.com/iHuman-Lab/mosaic.git
cd mosaic
conda create -n mosaic_env python=3.11 -y
conda activate mosaic_env
```

:::
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.line-steps}
::: {.line-step}
[1]{.line-num} [Download the code]{.line-title}

Clones the MOSAIC repository
:::
::: {.line-step}
[2]{.line-num} [Enter the folder]{.line-title}

Stay in `mosaic` for the whole tutorial
:::
::: {.line-step}
[3]{.line-num} [Create the environment]{.line-title}

A private Python named `mosaic_env`
:::
::: {.line-step}
[4]{.line-num} [Activate it]{.line-title}

Every later command runs inside it
:::
:::
:::

::::

::: {.checkpoint}
Your prompt begins with `(mosaic_env)`, and `python --version` reports 3.10 or 3.11.
:::

::: {.notes}
Choose either venv or Conda, not both. Ubuntu attendees who see "ensurepip is not
available" should install python3-venv, delete the incomplete mosaic_env, and
repeat the step. PowerShell needs the leading dot-backslash on the activation
script. Everyone stays in the mosaic directory for the rest of the tutorial.
:::

## Install [MOSAIC]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Three commands, run from the `mosaic` folder with `mosaic_env` active.
:::

:::: {.columns .install-split}

::: {.column width="60%"}
```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e .
python -c "import mosaic.sar.env, mosaic.gui.main; print('MOSAIC ready')"
```

::: {.checkpoint}
pip ends with `Successfully installed ... mosaic-0.1.0`, and the check prints a `pygame-ce` banner, then `MOSAIC ready`.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.line-steps}
::: {.line-step}
[1]{.line-num} [Update pip]{.line-title}

Avoids install errors from an old installer
:::
::: {.line-step}
[2]{.line-num} [Install MOSAIC]{.line-title}

Adds MOSAIC and every package on the previous slide. `-e` (editable) means your own code edits take effect without reinstalling.
:::
::: {.line-step}
[3]{.line-num} [Check it]{.line-title}

Imports the task (`mosaic.sar`) and the participant's interface (`mosaic.gui`)
:::
:::
:::

::::

---

## Installation [Checkpoint]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Part Two is done when the check prints `MOSAIC ready`.
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="38%"}
::: {.check-card}
[Confirm]{.check-title}

::: {.check-item}
Your prompt begins with `(mosaic_env)`
:::
::: {.check-item}
pip ended with `Successfully installed ... mosaic-0.1.0`
:::
::: {.check-item}
The import check printed `MOSAIC ready`
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="62%"}
::: {.tight-table}

| Symptom | Recovery |
|---|---|
| `No module named 'mosaic'` | Activate `mosaic_env`, rerun `pip install -e .` |
| `python --version` shows 3.9 or older | Recreate `mosaic_env` with Python 3.10 or 3.11 |
| PowerShell will not load `mosaic_env` | Run `.\mosaic_env\Scripts\Activate.ps1`; the leading `.\` is required |
| `ensurepip is not available` | Install `python3-venv`, recreate `mosaic_env` |

:::
:::

::::

::: {.punchline}
Everyone who sees `MOSAIC ready` is installed. Next, we [run it]{.accent}.
:::

::: {.notes}
Part Two ends at verification: nobody launches the game yet. Hold here until most
attendees see MOSAIC ready. Less common failures are on the appendix's
installation recovery slide while helpers work with individual machines.
:::

The first launch belongs to Part Three: this is the included study composition in
src/experiment/main.py, run from the cloned repository with no extra file. Hold
here until most attendees can move the agent. The terminal fills with pygame_gui
font warnings and "Timeout during mission generation: connect_all failed" lines
on every launch; both are harmless (the level generator retries). If it fails:
`No module named 'experiment'` means run from the repository root with
PYTHONPATH=src; no window or `No available video device` means a remote session,
so use a local laptop; `NameError: name 'LavaRiskVictimPlacer'` means the clone
predates the import fix, so `git pull`.
:::

## The SAR [Mission]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Rescue the real victims, avoid decoys and lava, and beat the clock.
:::

:::: {.columns .scenario-columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}
![](assets/gameplay.gif){fig-alt="The real interface: the agent rescues a real victim (green flash), then a decoy (red flash), then another real victim." height="360" fig-align="center"}
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
::: {.world-rail .mission-rail}

::: {.world-item}
![](assets/sprites/victim-real.png)

## How `experiment.main` Assembles [the Experiment]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
`src/experiment/main.py` is the composition point for the included study.
:::

:::: {.columns .compose-split}

::: {.src}
[`src/experiment/main.py` · simplified: building size and YAML lookups left out]{.src-cap}

::: {.compose-code}
```{.python code-line-numbers="|1-7|9|11|13"}
env = build_sar_env(
    screen_size=800,
    victim_placer=LavaRiskVictimPlacer(...),
    lava_placer=SectorSpreadLavaPlacer(...),
    locked_room_placer=LockedRoomPlacer(locked_room_prob=0.5),
    camera_strategy=AgentFOVCamera(),
)

teammate = build_llm_client(provider=config.get("provider", "dummy"))

gui = SAREnvGUI(env, config=config, llm_client=teammate)

gui.run()
```
:::

::: {.punchline}
`experiment.main` selects and connects the components. [The reusable implementations remain in `mosaic`.]{.accent}
:::

::: {.notes}
This is the included study composition used for the tutorial, not the only way to
use MOSAIC: any script can import the same pieces and connect them differently.
Step through the highlights; each number on the right is one highlight. The exact
lines (31–51, with the building size and the YAML lookups) are on the appendix's
Mission Composition slide. There is no rewards argument in this call: scoring
uses RescueRewards' defaults (+1 / −1 / −2) unless you pass
action=RescueAction(rewards=...). This is main.py as the tutorial needs it,
imports enabled and the provider defaulting to "dummy"; upstream must carry that
fix before the session.
:::

## Where Changes Are [Made]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Each research decision maps to one area of MOSAIC.
:::

::: {.decision-map}

| Research decision | MOSAIC area | Examples | Lives in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Task performed by the participant | SAR | Victims, hazards, rewards, time | `mosaic.sar` · `experiment/placers.py` |
| Information available to the participant | GUI | Camera, panels, feedback | `mosaic.core.camera` · `mosaic.gui` |
| Behavior of the AI teammate | AI interface | Provider, reliability, timing, prompt | `mosaic.llm` · `experiment/llm.py` |
| Information recorded by the study | Sensing and logging | Actions, advice, gaze, outcomes | `mosaic.sar.observations` · `experiment/sensors/` |

:::

::: {.punchline}
The appendix has a worked change for each area. Part Four uses [all four in one study]{.accent}.
:::

::: {.notes}
One map instead of a tour of settings. The time limit is a task decision but is
read by the GUI (`max_time` in `SAREnvGUI`); advice timing is read there too
(`llm_nudge_interval`). The appendix keeps the one-setting tasks (counts, locked
rooms, rewards, time, cameras, feedback, info panel, teammate, timing, prompts,
records) for anyone who wants to try them after the session.
:::

[Part Four notebook · planned]{.code-file}

```{.python code-line-numbers="false"}

```
:::

::: {.lives-in}
[Lives in]{.task-label} `src/mosaic/llm/client.py` · `LLMClient.query(prompt)`

The lab-hosted service provides the LLM connection. Its key never reaches the notebook.
:::
:::

::: {.result-col}
[How each piece of advice is made]{.task-label}

::: {.compose-map}

::: {.compose-row}
[1]{.compose-num} [Correct or not]{.compose-what}

The experiment decides, with probability set by reliability.
:::

::: {.compose-row}
[2]{.compose-num} [Target]{.compose-what}

The experiment picks it: a real victim, or a decoy.
:::

::: {.compose-row}
[3]{.compose-num} [Message]{.compose-what}

The LLM phrases that recommendation in natural language.
:::

::: {.compose-row}
[4]{.compose-num} [Record]{.compose-what}

MOSAIC logs the target, correctness, message, and response.
:::

:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
An uncontrolled LLM does not produce a set reliability, so the experiment makes
steps 1 and 2 and the LLM only does step 3. Steps 1 and 2 are what
labs/advisor.py's ReliableTeammate already does without an LLM: the nearest
reachable real victim, or with probability 1 − reliability the nearest decoy.
The provider key stays behind a lab-controlled service with rate and cost limits;
detailed provider setup is in the appendix.
:::

## Run the [Conditions]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Two short trials. Only the teammate's reliability changes.
:::

::: {.protocol-sequence .two-up}

::: {.protocol-stage}
[Condition A]{.protocol-title}

**Reliable advice** · `teammate_reliability = 1.0`

Play one short trial, and decide each time whether to follow the advice.
:::

::: {.protocol-stage .secondary}
[Condition B]{.protocol-title}

**Imperfect advice** · `teammate_reliability = 0.7`

Play the same mission again, with the same instructions.
:::

:::

::: {.cycle-band}
[Held constant]{.cycle-title} Same mission · same seed · same camera · same advice timing
:::

::: {.punchline}
A formal experiment would counterbalance condition order. Today [demonstrates the workflow]{.accent}; it is not a completed study.
:::

::: {.notes}
Show the procedure, not results. Playing B second on a layout already seen is a
learning effect; a real study counterbalances order across participants and
usually uses matched layouts. Keep advice timing identical in both conditions,
whichever way the notebook delivers advice.
:::

## Detailed Installation [Recovery]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Additional recovery steps for less common installation failures.
:::

| Symptom | Recovery |
|---|---|
| `ensurepip is not available` | Install `python3-venv`, recreate `mosaic_env` |
| `python --version` reports 3.9 or older | Recreate `mosaic_env` on Python 3.10 or 3.11 |
| `pip install -e .` fails to build a wheel | Rerun `python -m pip install --upgrade pip`, then retry |
| `conda activate` does nothing in PowerShell | Run `conda init powershell` once, reopen the terminal |
| Mission window opens on the wrong monitor | Press `F11` to leave fullscreen and drag it |

rate by distance to lava; the study env `TunedPickupVictimEnv` drains victims in
view each step and emits `victim_died` at zero. The bar is drawn only while
advice is on screen (the study reveals it on each reply). In the tutorial's
`experiment.main` run, health does not drain.

[What it knows]{.more-title}

[The function that turns the game state into the teammate's prompt. The default lists every object, even ones out of view.]{.more-what}

```{.python code-line-numbers="false"}
SAREnvGUI(..., prompt_builder=my_builder)
```
:::

:::

::: {.result-terminal}
```{.text code-line-numbers="false"}
Agent: room (0,1) facing West | Carrying: nothing | …

Object       Direction  Visible  Reachable  PathLength
Victim4      East       Yes      Yes        9
Victim2      South      Yes      Yes        0
RedKey1      East       Yes      Yes        5
PurpleKey1   East       Yes      Yes        6
PurpleDoor1  South      Yes      Yes        34
RedDoor1     East       No       Yes        10
```
:::
:::

::: {.more-row}
::: {.more-text}
[How it speaks]{.more-title}

[`sparse` asks for one short instruction; `detailed`, the default, for a short briefing. LLM teammates only: it needs a hosted model and an API key.]{.more-what}

::: {.code-card .mini}
[`configs/experiment.yaml`]{.code-file} [a new top-level line]{.code-where}

```{.yaml code-line-numbers="false"}
prompt_type: sparse
```
:::

[Interpret]{.var-label} how much advice per message
:::

::: {.speech-pair}
::: {.speech}
[detailed · the default, up to 40 words]{.result-label}

“Survivor to your South — get there fast, then swing North for the second one. The locked door East needs the yellow key first.”
:::

::: {.speech}
[sparse · one sentence, up to 20 words]{.result-label}

“Survivor to your South — pick them up now, then head North for the next one.”
:::
:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
The table is the start of what MOSAIC's default prompt builder (`build_obs` in
src/mosaic/llm/process_prompts.py) sends, trimmed to five of its columns; it
lists every object, including ones outside the participant's view. A
`prompt_builder=` function replaces it with whatever you choose to send. The two
quotes are the example replies in MOSAIC's prompt templates
(src/mosaic/llm/prompts.yaml); `prompt_type` applies to LLM teammates. A
`response_processor=` function rewrites every reply before it is shown.
:::

## AI Teammate [Interface]{.accent}

::: {.hook}
Provider configuration lives outside the reusable task environment.

:::

```python
from mosaic.llm.client import LLMClient, DummyLLMClient, ask
```

```bash
pip install llama-index-llms-openai
pip install llama-index-llms-google-genai
```

```python
from experiment.llm import LlamaIndexLLMClient

teammate = LlamaIndexLLMClient("openai", "gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07")
# or: LlamaIndexLLMClient("google", "gemini-2.5-flash")

SAREnvGUI(env, llm_client=teammate).run()
```

::: {.note}
The reusable package defines the client contract. The study layer selects the provider and model. A provider needs its matching package and environment key; if advice fails, the mission remains playable and the chat panel reports the error.
:::
